verdict.rationale: GrowthBook ships an official MCP server that connects AI tools like Cursor, VS Code, and Claude to the product. It loads GrowthBook Agent Skills (workflows and guardrails) and makes authenticated REST API calls, so users can drive the product through natural-language prompts in an external AI client. The natural-language layer comes from that third-party assistant, not from GrowthBook, and the Cmd+K palette is navigation rather than natural-language commands. Missing for 10: an in-product natural-language command interface, documentation of which operations are reachable via natural language, and hands-on or independent corroboration of the natural-language workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Connect AI tools like Cursor, VS Code, and Claude to GrowthBook using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
The official GrowthBook MCP server is a thin bridge: it loads GrowthBook Agent Skills (workflows and guardrails) and makes authenticated calls to the GrowthBook REST API.
